problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ There exists $y\in R$ such that $\frac{y}{2}$ is not real.
worked_solution:
If we denote

$$
P(y):\frac{y}{2}\text{ is real},
$$

our statement can be written as

$$
∃y\in R,\,¬P(y).
$$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∃y\in R,\,¬P(y)) & ≡∀y\in R,\,¬¬P(y) \\  & ≡∀y\in R,\,P(y).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $∀y\in R,\,P(y)$ reads as follows:

$\,$ **For all** $y\in R,$ $\frac{y}{2}$ is real.

choices.value: For all $y\in R,$ $\frac{y}{2}$ is not real.
There exists $y\in R$ such that $\frac{y}{2}$ is real.
